short: the hub's page, a Svelte and Vite project
is: The Svelte application `zaf hub --port <n>` serves at `/`, built by Vite into a committed dist/ that the zaf binary embeds at compile time.
conventions: Commit dist/ in the same change as the source it was built from; commit package-lock.json when a dependency changes
Built files have fixed names (assets/app.js, assets/app.css, set in vite.config.js); a build that makes another file fails cargo's `every_built_file_is_served` until assets.rs lists it
The page loads nothing from outside the hub's server
`npm ci`, `npm run build`, `npm test` (Vitest on jsdom) from zaf/web; cargo never needs Node

fs.name: dist/
fs.role: the committed build (index.html, assets/app.js, assets/app.css), embedded by zaf/src/app/hub/dashboard/assets.rs; never edited by hand

fs.name: index.html
fs.role: the page's shell that Vite builds from

fs.name: package.json
fs.role: zaf-hub-page, private: dev, build and test scripts; Svelte 5, Vite 6, Vitest 3, Testing Library, jsdom

fs.name: src/
fs.role: components, the hub's API client and their tests

fs.name: vite.config.js
fs.role: fixed output names, the dev proxy of /api to a hub on port 7777, the Vitest setup

notes: `npm run dev` needs a running `zaf hub --port 7777` in a project
The JSON it reads and the controls it posts to are served by zaf/src/app/hub/ (dashboard.rs, controls/)
No term of the type vocabulary is nearer than code for a web front end
